evidence: src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts: execute() checks `if (!isOrderStatus(targetStatus)) throw new DomainError("VALIDATION", "Unknown order status")`

src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts: validateExecute(status) checks `if (!isOrderStatus(status)) throw new DomainError("VALIDATION", "Query parameter 'status' must be a valid order status")`. This repeats the same check inside the same class, with a different message

src/application/list-orders-use-case.ts: execute(status) has the identical check `if (!isOrderStatus(status)) throw new DomainError("VALIDATION", "Query parameter 'status' must be a valid order status")`
src/application/get-stock-levels-use-case.ts maps products to StockLevelDto inline, while the order use cases use toOrderDto from order-mapper.ts. StockLevelDto is declared in order-dto.ts
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Overall the module holds together: it is the application layer for order and stock use cases, and the order use cases all go through the shared toOrderDto mapper and the DTOs in order-dto.ts. The problem is the order-status validation rule. It is implemented in several places with different error messages. AdvanceOrderUseCase also exposes validateExecute, a method that validates a query parameter. That method copies ListOrdersUseCase's check word for word, including the "Query parameter 'status'" message, which belongs to listing orders and has nothing to do with advancing one. So the same invariant lives in more than one place, and a list-query concern has leaked into the advance use case. Two smaller issues: GetStockLevelsUseCase builds StockLevelDto inline instead of using a mapper, and StockLevelDto is declared in order-dto.ts. Both are minor.

violations.message: validateExecute(status) copies ListOrdersUseCase's order-status query-parameter check, message included, and also repeats the isOrderStatus check already done in execute() with a different message. The status-validation rule is implemented in several places, and a list-query concern has leaked into the advance use case.
execute() implements the same isOrderStatus validation, with the same error message, that AdvanceOrderUseCase.validateExecute duplicates. The rule should live in one place.
